bodycorp.name: Body corporates and unit title complexes
bodycorp.desc: Body corporates, unit title blocks, apartments and townhouse complexes
profile: Weathertightness defects, remedial works or a leaky building history?
Earthquake-prone notice, or seismic assessment below 34% NBS?
Valuation date and who did it
Long-term maintenance plan and sinking fund in place?

gen: Unit Titles Act requires cover for full replacement. Check the valuation is under 3 years old, includes demolition, fees and code upgrades, and covers common property and fixtures.
Owners insure contents and their own fit-out. Check what the body corporate policy covers inside units and the excess split.
mdamage: Burst pipes and leaks between units dominate claims. Check the excess per claim, who pays it, and whether the body corporate can recover it from owners.
Check cover for earthquake, flood and land slip, and the basis of cover for any cladding or remedial works.
liab: Common areas
Lifts, car parks, pools, balconies and gyms. Ask about maintenance contracts, inspections and incident records.
dno: Committee members can be personally challenged. Check cover for the committee and the manager, and for disputes between owners.
crime: Levies held in bank accounts. Check dual authorisation, who controls the account and cover for the manager's staff.

docs: Unit title plan and schedule of units

finishtrades.name: Floor layers, tilers, insulation and fencing
finishtrades.desc: Flooring, tiling, insulation installation, fencing, decking and similar finishing trades
profile: Wet area waterproofing or shower membranes installed?
Moisture testing of slabs and subfloors before laying?
Work on pre-2000 buildings where asbestos or lead may be present?
Share of work in new builds (%)

liab: Leaks and moisture failures
Failed shower membranes, subfloor moisture and sealant failures show up months or years later. Ask about product warranties, producer statements and inspection records.
Insulation and fire
Wrong products near downlights, flues and wiring cause fires. Check product standards, installer certification and clearance procedures.
Fence and boundary disputes
Fences built on the wrong boundary or damaging services. Ask about surveys, dial-before-you-dig and neighbour consents.
gen: Many finishing trades use sub-contractors and day labour. Check their insurance, licences and written agreements.

demolition.name: Demolition, asbestos removal and waste
demolition.desc: Demolition, asbestos removal, hazardous waste, skip bins and recycling
profile: Work next to occupied buildings, roads or services?
Waste disposed at consented facilities with records kept?
Fire risk controls at transfer stations or storage yards (stockpiles, batteries)?

liab: Adjoining property damage
Collapse, vibration and dust affecting neighbours. Check removal-of-support, vibration and underpinning exclusions.
Pollution and asbestos
Asbestos fibre release, contaminated waste and leaching. Many policies exclude pollution; ask for sudden and accidental cover and a clear asbestos position.
Hired and owned plant
Excavators with demolition attachments, trucks and skip loaders. Check operator competence and hire agreements.
mdamage: Combustible waste, lithium batteries and scrap yards are a growing fire cause. Ask about separation, monitoring and fire plans.
statutory: Licensing, air monitoring and clearance certificates. Check defence cost cover and history of notices.

ruralcontract.name: Rural contractors
ruralcontract.desc: Shearing, spraying, baling, silage, cultivation, fencing and other farm contracting
profile: Spraying or spreading near neighbours, waterways or crops?
Number of tractors, harvesters and self-propelled machines
Hired-in operators or contract drivers used?
Large machinery moved on public roads?

liab: Spray drift and spreading damage
Drift onto neighbouring crops, stock and waterways is the classic claim. Ask about certification, records, wind rules and buffer distances.
Fire from harvesting
Baling, header and silage machinery start crop and paddock fires. Check fire exclusions in the policy and fire-fighting equipment on machines.
Damage to customers' property
Damaged fences, pasture, irrigation lines and stock. Check exclusions for property in your care, custody and control.
mdamage: Tractors, balers and self-propelled machines are high value. Check agreed value, seasonal peaks and hired-in plant.
statutory: Rollovers, PTO entanglements and stock handling. Check training records and notices.

fishing.name: Fishing, aquaculture and marine farming
fishing.desc: Commercial fishing vessels, mussel, oyster and salmon farms, and seafood harvesting
profile: Value of vessels and farm structures ($)
Crew employed under written agreements with safety training?
Consents, permits and quota held and current?
Chilled or frozen stock held ashore?

gen: Vessels need hull and machinery cover separate from the business policy. Check survey dates, agreed value, trading limits and crew qualifications.
Lines, anchors, pens and floats. Ask about storm damage, mooring survey, theft and loss of stock.
liab: Pollution and spills
Fuel and waste discharge from vessels and farms. Check marine pollution cover and consent breaches.
statutory: Maritime NZ and WorkSafe rules apply to crew and vessels. Check safety systems and defence cost cover.
cargo: Catch and product moved to market or export. Check the temperature breakdown and spoilage position.

marine.name: Marinas, boat charter and boat builders
marine.desc: Marinas, boatyards, boat builders, charter and ferry operators
profile: Value of customers' boats in your care at peak ($)
Maximum passengers carried at one time
Vessels survey-compliant and skippers qualified for the trading area?
Fire controls in sheds and fuel dock (extinguishers, shore power, refuelling)?

liab: Boats in your care
Customers' boats on berths, hardstand or in the shed are in your care, custody and control. Ask about marina operator or bailee cover, and which perils apply.
Passengers
Injury to passengers or loss of life. Check the liability limit against vessel capacity and maritime law exclusions.
mdamage: Pontoons, piles and marina structures are exposed to storm and wave damage. Check the sum insured basis and storm limits.
Fibreglass, fuel and welding in sheds. Ask about fire controls, shore power and hot work procedures.

tourism.name: Tourism and adventure operators
tourism.desc: Guided tours, adventure activities, wildlife and day experiences
profile: Adventure activity safety audit completed with WorkSafe-recognised operator certification?
Participants sign a waiver or acknowledgement of risk?

liab: Adventure activity exclusions
Many general liability policies exclude adventure and high-risk activities or cap them. Confirm each activity is listed and any limit or excess applies.
Waivers and participants
Waivers do not remove liability under the Accident Compensation Act and Fair Trading Act. Check the wording and participant instructions.
Overseas participants
Claims from overseas visitors may be brought outside NZ. Check jurisdiction and territorial limits.
statutory: Safety audits and registration. Check the current audit status and cover for defence costs.
fleet: Vans, buses and boats carrying clients. Check licence class and passenger limits.

hire.name: Equipment, plant and vehicle hire
hire.desc: Plant hire, tool hire, party hire, campervan and car rental
profile: Hire agreements transfer risk and require hirers' insurance or a damage waiver?
Number of hire vehicles on the road
Tracking or immobilisers on the hire fleet?

liab: Hirers' claims and training
Faulty or poorly explained equipment injuring hirers. Ask about inspection records, instruction and signed hire terms.
Plant hired to others
Cover for plant at others' sites and who insures against damage to it. Check hire agreement indemnities.
mdamage: Theft and damage of hired items
Check the basis of valuation, theft from sites and the excess. A damage waiver sold to hirers needs matching cover.
fleet: Rental and campervan fleets: excess reduction products, overseas drivers, licence checks and damage waivers.

quarry.name: Quarries, aggregates and ready-mix
quarry.desc: Quarries, aggregate supply, concrete batching and ready-mix plants
profile: Wash water, silt or dust discharge consents in place?
Concrete or aggregates supplied under quality standards with test records?

liab: Product failure
Concrete or aggregate that fails strength tests can lead to large rework claims. Ask about batch testing, certificates and product liability limit.
Blasting and vibration
Neighbours' buildings and services. Check exclusions for blasting and removal of support.
Pollution and silt
Silt, wash water and fuel discharge. Check pollution cover and consent compliance.
mdamage: Crushers, screens and batching plants are high value and exposed to breakdown. Ask about maintenance, spares and indemnity period.
statutory: Quarries have dedicated safety regulations and managers. Check notices and defence cost cover.

valuers.name: Valuers, building inspectors and surveyors
valuers.desc: Property valuers, pre-purchase inspectors, quantity surveyors and compliance inspectors
profile: Registered with the relevant body or licensing scheme with current certificates?
Valuations relied on by banks or lenders?
Standard terms disclaiming reliance by third parties and defining scope?
Inspections include destructive or invasive testing?

pi: Banks, buyers and insurers rely on reports. Check disclaimers, scope limits and who may rely.
Hidden defects, weathertightness and asbestos missed in pre-purchase reports. Ask about report scope and photos.
Valuation and building claims can arise years later. Check the retroactive date and run-off.

events.name: Events, venues and wedding operators
events.desc: Event venues, function centres, wedding planners, festivals and hire
profile: Event cancellation or non-appearance cover needed for events held?
Security or crowd controllers used for larger events?
Suppliers (caterers, stage, rides) hold their own cover?

liab: Crowd injury and structures
Falls from stages, marquee collapse in wind and crowd crush. Check engineering sign-off, wind plans and the limit against capacity.
Liquor and food
Alcohol service and food safety. Check host responsibility and licence compliance.
Suppliers and hire-ins
Make sure caterers, stage hire and amusement suppliers carry insurance and indemnify you.
bi: Weather, illness and venue failure. General policies exclude these, so ask for event cancellation cover separately with the exact exclusions.
